Sl. 17. परिचरितव्याः—should be attended upon. यद्यपि &c.—
i. e. if they do not give special instruction &c. न—It will be
better to read नो to suit the metre. स्वैरकथाः—randam talk;
स्वेन ईरं ईरति वा । पचाद्यच् । शास्त्राणि—precepts, information that
can be safely relied upon.

transcription.note: Several Sanskrit words, particularly the grammatical explanation on line 4, are difficult to read.

lines.text: Sl. 18. कन्दुकपातेन—a curious phrase probably used for the
metre; the regular one would be कन्दुकपातं पतति, in the manner
of the fall of a ball i. e. to rise again. केन तुल्यं कन्दुकपातेन कन्दु-
कपातवत् यथा कन्दुकः पतन्नुत्पतति । Râmarshi. Cf. प्रायेण साधुवृत्तानां &c.
supra sl. 86. आर्यः—An honourable man, a man of merit. मृत्पिण्ड—
a lump of clay, which remains sticking to the ground and
never rises up.

transcription.note: The Sanskrit quotation on lines 3–4 is somewhat unclear.

lines.text: Sl. 19. अवकर m. sweepings, dust: from अवकॄ+अ (अप्,
अवकीर्यते इति ). कुक्कुट—कुकेन गलेन वक्रीति a cock. हंसः—a word
of the पृषोदरादि class; fr. हन् to go or हस्; भवेद्वर्णागमाद्धंसः ( the
न् or स् comes in irregularly ). Fig. अप्रस्तुतप्रशंसा.

transcription.note: Several Sanskrit etymological forms are indistinct.

lines.text: Sl. 20. मदभिन्न V. l.—In this case गण्ड must be taken in the
sense of cheeks, and करट the frontal globes. निद्रालसाः—dull with
the nightly sleep. वीणा &c.—For the idea expressed here, comp.
Kir. I. 38. and Rag. V. 65. सुरलोकदेव—the lord of the world
of gods i. e. Indra; or it may mean the gods of heaven. सदृशं—
qualifies तदैश्वर्यं understood. विस्फूर्जितं—properly a flash of light-
ning; hence manifestation. Construe नागाः निद्रालसाः तिष्ठन्ति इति
यत् &c.—When the relative stands for a whole sentence such as
is represented by ‘that’ in English, it is always used in the
sing. number and neuter gender. See Apte’s Guide. § 25. The
fig. is उदात्त which is described as उदात्तं वस्तुनः संपत् the descrip-
tion of the excellence of a thing.

transcription.note: Some Sanskrit words are indistinct, especially on lines 1 and 5–7.

lines.text: Sl. 21. परोपकारित्वम्—परस्य उपकरोतीति परोपकारी तस्य भावः ।
द्वितयम् । See com. and Pân. V. 2. 42. quoted therein.

transcription.note: The first Sanskrit word on line 2 is somewhat unclear.
